Fort Churchill's military authorities commenced a search with the aid of helicopters and aircraft. On September 21, the two boats used by the men were located; both were undamaged and swamped. Numerous items belonging to the four men were found. Despite extensive land and water searches, the bodies were not found.

Jacket: Nylon, Red, Black, Hip length, black on the back of sleeves

Case reference: 2014001469.CaseDesc: On November 28,1988, Douglas Babineau was seen for the last time at a party located on First Avenue in Moncton, New Brunswick. Douglas has not been seen or heard from since.

Case reference: 2017023444.CaseDesc: June Pauline Stevens went missing in July 1948 while living in Cadillac, Saskatchewan, and has not been heard from since. It was speculated that she had travelled west to Port Alberni in British Columbia to join her mother, or to Winnipeg, Manitoba, to join other relatives.

Case reference: 2017065923.CaseDesc: Oleg Chmelev was last seen at his home in the area of Morning Star Drive and Brandon Gate Drive, Mississauga, on October 30, 2017. His green bicycle was also missing and was his main mode of transportation.

Case reference: 2019052051.CaseDesc: On September 10, 2019, at approximately 4:00 am, Brandon Pollock was seen for the last time at his family residence in Hamilton, Ontario. That same morning, three men on a boat observed a man swimming in the area of the Lift Bridge in Lake Ontario. The men approached the swimmer, who was later identified as Brandon Pollock, to confirm his wellbeing. Brandon had told them that he was okay and advised them to pass by.

Mark: Right Side Of Neck, A brown birthmark on the right side of the neck, below the ear

Case reference: 2014030665.CaseDesc: On January 19, 1978, the partial remains of a female believed to be aged between 55-70 years of age, were found in the waters of the Salish Sea, southwest of Victoria, British Columbia. She had moderate arthritis and significant healed injuries to her left ankle and foot. It is believed she was deceased several months or even years before her remains were recovered

Case reference: 2017047885.CaseDesc: On July 31, 2017, Brayden Thibault was seen for the last time when he left Fredericton, New Brunswick to meet someone in the city of Moncton, New Brunswick. Brayden has not been seen or heard from since.

Case reference: 2019010367.CaseDesc:
Simeon Bear was last seen on July 23, 1982 when he was last seen boating on Reindeer Lake,
heading out from Southend, Saskatchewan to Lawrence Bay during a storm.

Deformity: Right Hand, Disfigured index, middle and ring fingers

Case reference: 2008018199.CaseDesc: Carl Braum and Thomas Lumsden were last seen on the morning of May 19, 1974. They were travelling in a 14-foot fibreglass canoe in a northerly direction in the area of Depot Harbour, Wasauksing First Nation, Parry Sound District, Ontario. They were believed to be travelling to Killbear Provincial Park. There were no life jackets in the canoe.

Case reference: 2013000142.CaseDesc: Richard Dryland was known to be homeless in the Grande Prairie, Alberta area. Richard's lifestyle was characterised by its transient nature, with frequent travel to British Columbia. In November 1993, he was released from the Peace River Correctional Centre. His family have been unable to make contact with him since that time.

Tattoo: Right Upper Arm, Heart and dagger

Case reference: 2016006283.CaseDesc: Larry Legacey was reported missing on March 22, 1993 when friends and family had not heard from him in several weeks. He was last known to reside in Edmonton, Alberta, but also frequented the Round Hill area, southeast of Edmonton. He also frequently traveled to Calgary, Alberta and to British Columbia.

Tattoo: Left Upper Arm, Eagle and text "DAD HARLEY"

Case reference: 2014003981.CaseDesc: On September 15, 1978, Wayne Kevin Spark was last seen in Richmond, British Columbia. Wayne left home to attend Vancouver Community College but never showed up. Wayne has not been seen or heard from since.
